verdict.rationale: OpenTofu's own docs say configurations are code that can be versioned. Its speculative `tofu plan` lets developers preview changes before code review, and plans can be saved with `-out` and applied later. That covers the version and review parts of the story. Rollback is not documented: destroy mode tears down everything rather than restoring a prior state, and reverting via git is a user-side workaround. missing for 10: a documented rollback or restore-to-previous-state capability, independent hands-on corroboration of version/review workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: This allows a blueprint of your datacenter to be versioned and treated as you would any other code.
human-readable configuration files that you can version, reuse, and share
developers can use speculative plans to verify the effect of their changes before submitting them for code review
You can use the optional `-out=FILE` option to save the generated plan to a file on disk, which you can later execute by passing the file to `tofu apply` as an extra argument.
